subject.title: [Feature]: Support plugin-requestable session isolation for trust boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-requestable quarantined execution as a public Plugin SDK/runtime contract, and what enforceable guarantees should that contract make?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but the permanent API shape changes security boundaries, session semantics, and public Plugin SDK expectations that automation should not decide.

options.title: Keep As Design Item
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define isolation semantics, trust metadata, prerequisite hook context, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Primitives
options.body: Defer the hook directive and document current sessions_spawn sandbox patterns as the supported workaround for trusted operators.

options.title: Reject Plugin-Requested Isolation
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers decide strong mixed-trust isolation must stay at separate gateway, OS-user, or host boundaries.

recommendation.title: Keep As Design Item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define isolation semantics, trust metadata, prerequisite hook context, and compatibility expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is recent ownership of subagent context/thread behavior and adjacent security-sensitive runtime/plugin seams.
